bug_semantics: The default object.to_json builtin recursively serialized IList/array elements and accessible object members through a static local WriteValue function without a recursion-depth limit, execution-stack guard, or circular-reference check. A template-controlled ScriptObject can refer to itself and be passed to object.to_json, causing WriteValue to revisit the same object until a fatal StackOverflowException terminates the hosting .NET process; sufficiently deep acyclic input reaches the same uncontrolled-recursion path.
flaw_origin: PR #533 member commit a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f is the smallest commit that first added ToJson, WriteValue, and both unchecked recursive calls in src/Scriban/Functions/ObjectFunctions.cs. Its immediate parent lacks the entire implementation. The later one-parent squash f2f3cf41cde1ba7226760fd9b456f3d5d7aa1ca1 is an aggregate rather than the BIC: the retained PR chain is reconstructable, the final member and squash have identical trees, and the vulnerable file blob written by a65c891245e2c8550fb28fcd6e9d296c99ad6a2f landed unchanged.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p on the BIC commit object identifies René Larch <renelarch@gmail.com> as both author and committer, and its feat subject plus three implementation bullets contain no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, Copilot, bot identity, or other AI marker.
